Great question. Langfuse is an open‑source AI engineering platform for building, debugging, and improving LLM apps and agents. It helps with:

  • Observability & tracing: Capture every prompt, model response, tool/retrieval step, latency, tokens, and errors to debug complex chains/agents Docs: Observability overview
  • Evaluation: Score output quality via LLM‑as‑a‑judge, code evaluators, human review, and user feedback—both on production traces (online) and datasets (offline) Docs: Evaluation overview, Core concepts
  • Prompt management: Version, release/rollback, test in a playground, and link prompts to traces and scores—update prompts without code deploys Docs: Prompt mgmt overview
  • Analytics, dashboards & alerts: Track quality, latency, cost, volume; alert on regressions (e.g., hallucination rate, error spikes) Docs: Custom dashboards, Alerts
  • Cost & token tracking: Break down usage and USD cost per model/provider Docs
  • Users, sessions, releases: Attribute traces to users/sessions, segment by env/version for safer rollouts Docs
  • OpenTelemetry-native & integrations: Works with Python/JS SDKs and 100+ frameworks/models; can ingest from existing OTel setups Docs
  • Deployment & security: Cloud or self-hosted (MIT OSS), with enterprise options and compliance controls Overview, Security, Self-hosting

Try it quickly:

  • Set up your first trace: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started
  • Explore the platform overview: https://langfuse.com/docs

Would you like me to map these to your specific use case (e.g., chatbot, RAG, agent, or code generation) so we can suggest the fastest setup path?

Great question. Langfuse is an open‑source AI engineering platform for building, debugging, and improving LLM apps and agents. It helps with:

  • Observability & tracing: Capture every prompt, model response, tool/retrieval step, latency, tokens, and errors to debug complex chains/agents Docs: Observability overview
  • Evaluation: Score output quality via LLM‑as‑a‑judge, code evaluators, human review, and user feedback—both on production traces (online) and datasets (offline) Docs: Evaluation overview, Core concepts
  • Prompt management: Version, release/rollback, test in a playground, and link prompts to traces and scores—update prompts without code deploys Docs: Prompt mgmt overview
  • Analytics, dashboards & alerts: Track quality, latency, cost, volume; alert on regressions (e.g., hallucination rate, error spikes) Docs: Custom dashboards, Alerts
  • Cost & token tracking: Break down usage and USD cost per model/provider Docs
  • Users, sessions, releases: Attribute traces to users/sessions, segment by env/version for safer rollouts Docs
  • OpenTelemetry-native & integrations: Works with Python/JS SDKs and 100+ frameworks/models; can ingest from existing OTel setups Docs
  • Deployment & security: Cloud or self-hosted (MIT OSS), with enterprise options and compliance controls Overview, Security, Self-hosting

Try it quickly:

  • Set up your first trace: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started

{"type": "text", "text": "# Langfuse\n\n> Langfuse is an **open-source AI engineering platform** ([GitHub](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse)) that helps teams collaboratively debug, analyze, and iterate on their LLM applications. All platform features are natively integrated to accelerate the development workflow.\n\n## Markdown Access\n\nEvery page on langfuse.com is available as plain Markdown. Append `.md` to any URL, or send an `Accept: text/markdown` header:\n\n```bash\ncurl https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started.md\n```\n\nThe links in the section indexes below already point at the `.md` variants.\n\n## Docs Search API\n\nSemantic search (RAG) over the Langfuse documentation, returning an answer with the relevant pages and excerpts. No authentication required. Use this instead of guessing when a specific page does not answer the question:\n\n```bash\ncurl -sG \"https://langfuse.com/api/search-docs\" --data-urlencode \"query=How do I trace a LangGraph agent?\"\n```\n\n- **Endpoint**: `https://langfuse.com/api/search-docs?query=<question>`\n- **Documentation**: [REST endpoint](https://langfuse.com/docs/docs-mcp#rest-endpoint)\n\nAsk specific, self-contained questions in natural language. This is the same search that backs the `searchLangfuseDocs` MCP tool below.\n\n## Langfuse Docs MCP Server\n\nConnect to the Langfuse Docs MCP server to access documentation directly in your AI editor:\n\n- **Endpoint**: `https://langfuse.com/api/mcp`\n- **Transport**: `streamableHttp`\n- **Documentation**: [Langfuse Docs MCP Server](https://langfuse.com/docs/docs-mcp)\n\nThe MCP server provides tools to search Langfuse documentation, GitHub issues, and discussions. See the [installation guide](https://langfuse.com/docs/docs-mcp) for setup instructions in Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop, and other MCP clients.\n\n## Langfuse Skill for AI Coding Agents\n\nInstall the Langfuse skill before implementing anything with Langfuse. The skill provides up-to-date documentation, best-practice workflows for instrumentation, prompt management, and programmatic API access via the Langfuse CLI.\n\nInstall from: [github.com/langfuse/skills](https://github.com/langfuse/skills/tree/main/skills/langfuse)\n\n## Tracing Best Practices\n\nBefore instrumenting an application with Langfuse, read [What does a good trace look like?](https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/best-practices.md) — it covers trace scope, observation naming, meaningful input/output, and the attributes (metadata, tags, users, sessions) that evaluators, dashboards, and experiments rely on.\n\n## Docs\n\nFor the best results, install the [Langfuse skill](https://github.com/langfuse/skills/tree/main/skills/langfuse) before using these docs.\n\nFor the full list with links to each page, see: https://langfuse.com/llms-docs.txt\n\nPages: Overview, Audit Logs, Authentication & SSO, Billable Units, Data Deletion, Data Retention, LLM Connections, Access Control (RBAC), SCIM and Org API, Spend Alerts, Troubleshooting and FAQ, Agent Skill, Blob storage export field reference, CLI, Experiments API, Export from UI, Export to blob {"type": "text", "text": "{\"content\": [{\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/faq/all/llm-observability\", \"title\": \"What is LLM Observability and LLM Monitoring?\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"What is LLM Observability & Monitoring? - Langfuse\\n[Faq](/faq)\\n[All FAQs](/faq/all)\\n[What is LLM Observability & Monitoring?](/faq/all/llm-observability)\\n# What is LLM Observability and LLM Monitoring?\\nAs large language models (LLMs) continue to transform the landscape of AI and software development, understanding their behavior and performance becomes crucial. This is where **LLM observability** and **LLM monitoring** come into play. Observability refers to the ability to monitor and understand the internal states of an LLM application through its outputs, helping developers ensure these systems operate effectively and efficiently.\\n## Why Do We Need LLM Observability?\\n### The Complexities of LLM Deployment\\nDeploying LLMs is not a straightforward task. It comes with a whole set of unique challenges that differ significantly from traditional software development. Many valuable LLM apps rely on **complex, repeated, chained, or agentic calls** to a foundation model. This intricate control flow can make debugging challenging, as it is not always easy to pinpoint the root cause of an issue. This is where observability really shines.\\n### Handling Non-Deterministic Outputs\\nAnother hurdle is the **unpredictable nature of LLMs**. Unlike traditional software, where outputs can be tested against expected results, LLMs generate variable outputs. This makes it difficult to consistently assess quality. Developers need innovative ways to evaluate and monitor the quality of LLM outputs, especially as models evolve and change outside of the user's control. This is where **LLM analytics** becomes essential.\\n### Dealing with Mixed Intent\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nLLM applications, especially those involving conversation, often contend with **widely varying inputs and user intents**. This poses a significant challenge for teams developing and testing these applications, as real-world users often have different goals than expected. Therefore, understanding user behavior and managing unexpected inputs become essential components of LLM observability.\\n## What Makes Up LLM Observability?\\n### Monitoring and Tracing\\nMonitoring involves keeping an eye on the performance and behavior of LLM apps in real-time. Key metrics include **latency, throughput, and error rates** to ensure everything runs smoothly. Tracing, on the other hand, captures detailed execution paths within the application. By tracing the flow of requests and responses, developers can identify bottlenecks and errors, gaining insights into how different components interact.\\n### Metrics and Evaluation\\nTo evaluate the quality of LLM outputs, developers need to define and track relevant metrics. These could include **model-based evaluations, user feedback, and manual labeling**. By collecting and analyzing these metrics, developers can monitor quality over time, understand user interactions, and refine their models accordingly. This helps in making informed decisions about model updates and deployments.\\n### Real-World Context Analysis\\nUnderstanding user behavior and intent is crucial for LLM applications. Observability enables developers to classify and analyze user inputs, helping them adapt their applications to real-world contexts. This involves gathering insights into **user behavior, preferences, and pain points** , ultimately improving the overall user experience.\\n## What Is an LLM Observability Platform?\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nAn **LLM observability platform** is a system that captures every request an LLM application handles and turns that data into something a team can debug, evaluate, and improve. It replaces a patchwork of log files, evaluation scripts, and prompt spreadsheets with one place where execution data, quality scores, and prompts live together.\\nFive capabilities define the category:\\nCapability| What it covers \\n---|--- \\nTracing| Records each request with its prompts, model responses, token usage, latency, and tool or retrieval steps. \\nEvaluation| Attaches quality scores to outputs via automated evaluators, human annotation, or user feedback. \\nPrompt management| Versions prompts centrally so they can be updated and rolled back without a code deployment. \\nCost tracking| Breaks down token usage and USD cost per model and usage type. \\nDashboards and metrics| Aggregates traces and scores into charts for latency, cost, error rates, and quality over time. \\n \\nLangfuse is an open-source example of this category. It captures traces of complete application runs, including nested tool and retrieval steps, and lets teams score them with automated and manual evaluators. [Prompt management](/docs/prompt-management) versions prompts outside the codebase and caches them client-side, so retrieving them adds no latency. [Token and cost tracking](/docs/observability/features/token-and-cost-tracking) infers usage and USD cost from the model name or accepts exact values ingested via SDKs and integrations. To try the platform, [set up your first trace](/docs/observability/get-started); it works with any model or framework, and you can adopt the remaining capabilities incrementally.\\n## How Do You Monitor LLM Outputs in Production?\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nYou monitor LLM outputs in production by attaching evaluation scores to live traces and then tracking, visualizing, and alerting on those scores, rather than reading individual outputs by hand. In Langfuse, four mechanisms work together:\\n**1.** **Online evaluation** scores live production traffic automatically. An [LLM-as-a-Judge evaluator](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/llm-as-a-judge) runs on incoming traces or observations and returns a numeric, categorical, or boolean score, for example a hallucination check that returns `true` or `false` per response.\\n**2.** **User feedback** captures whether outputs actually helped users. Explicit signals like thumbs up/down, star ratings, and comments, or implicit signals like retries and accepted suggestions, are stored as [scores linked to traces](/docs/observability/features/user-feedback), so you can filter for poorly rated interactions and inspect the full context.\\n**3.** **Dashboards** show how output quality develops over time. [Custom dashboards](/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards) chart score averages, cost, and latency from live data, with filters and breakdowns by model, user, environment, or score value.\\n**4.** **Alerts** notify you when a metric crosses a threshold, so a quality regression does not depend on someone watching a chart. [Alerts](/docs/observability/features/alerts) evaluate a metric over a time window, support warning and alert thresholds, and send notifications to Slack, trigger GitHub Actions, or call your own webhooks. As of July 2026, alerts also support boolean scores: the average of a boolean score is the share of `true` results, so you can alert when the rate of failed policy checks or detected hallucinations exceeds a limit you set.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nTogether these mechanisms form a loop: evaluators and users score outputs, dashboards reveal trends, and alerts turn those trends into actionable notifications.\\n## How Langfuse Makes LLM Observability Easy\\nLet's talk about **[Langfuse](/)** , the open-source AI engineering platform designed to tackle the challenges of LLM observability. Langfuse is **model and framework agnostic** , making it easy to integrate with various LLM applications.\\nLangfuse’s features enable teams to capture the full context of an LLM application, from inference and embedding retrieval to API usage. **[Client SDKs](/docs/sdk/overview)** and integrations simplify tracking interactions with internal systems, allowing developers to pinpoint problems quickly. For more details on how to get started with SDKs, check out the [Langfuse SDK documentation](/integrations).\\nLangfuse also simplifies quality evaluation by letting users attach scores to production traces and monitor quality over time. You can learn more about how to evaluate and monitor application quality [here](/docs/evaluation/overview). Plus, its ability to classify inputs and analyze user behavior provides valuable insights into user interactions, helping teams iterate on their applications effectively.\\nOne of the best parts? Langfuse is **incrementally adoptable** , so you can start with a single integration and expand to full tracing of complex chains and agents as needed. Check out the [documentation](/docs) for more on getting started with integrations.\\n**LLM observability** and **LLM monitoring** are essential for keeping LLM applications running smoothly and effectively. With **Langfuse** , developers have a powerful tool to collaboratively debug, analyze, and iterate on their LLM projects, making it a valuable asset in the ever-evolving world of AI and machine learning.\\n⭐️\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n **Stay updated:** Star Langfuse on [GitHub](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse) to get instant notifications about new releases.[](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse)\\n* * *\\n* * *\\nLast edited 8/20/2026\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/integrations/frameworks/google-adk\", \"title\": \"Integrate Langfuse with Google's Agent Development Kit\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Observability for Google Agent Development Kit with Langfuse - Langfuse\\n[Integrations](/integrations)\\n[Frameworks](/integrations/frameworks/agno-agents)\\n[Google ADK](/integrations/frameworks/google-adk)\\nThis is a Jupyter notebook\\n[Open on GitHub](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/blob/main/cookbook/integration_google_adk.ipynb)\\n[Run on Google Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/langfuse/langfuse-docs/blob/main/cookbook/integration_google_adk.ipynb)\\n# Integrate Langfuse with Google's Agent Development Kit\\nThis notebook demonstrates how to capture detailed traces from a [Google Agent Development Kit](https://github.com/google/adk-python) (ADK) application with **[Langfuse](https://langfuse.com)** using the OpenTelemetry (OTel) protocol.\\n> **Why Agent Development Kit?** \\n> [Google’s Agent Development Kit](https://developers.googleblog.com/en/agent-development-kit-easy-to-build-multi-agent-applications/) streamlines building, orchestrating, and tracing generative-AI agents out of the box, letting you move from prototype to production far faster than wiring everything yourself.\\n> **Why Langfuse?** \\n> [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com) gives you a detailed dashboard and rich analytics for every prompt, model response, and function call in your agent, making it easy to debug, evaluate, and iterate on LLM apps.\\n**What this cookbook covers.** We start with the simplest possible trace and add one concept at a time:\\n 1. A hello-world agent with a tool call (Example 1)\\n 2. Named, filterable traces with tags and metadata (Example 2)\\n 3. A multi-agent pipeline whose trace shows every sub-agent (Example 3)\\n 4. Attaching user-feedback scores to a trace (Example 4)\\n## Step 1: Install dependencies\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n _Note:`google-adk` 2.x requires Python ≥ 3.10. The `\\\"google-adk>=2\\\"` pin ensures pip installs the current ADK 2.x release instead of resolving to an older 1.x version to satisfy OpenTelemetry version constraints._\\n \\n \\n```\\n%pip install langfuse \\\"google-adk>=2\\\" openinference-instrumentation-google-adk -q\\n```\\n## Step 2: Set up environment variables\\nFill in the **Langfuse** and your **Gemini API key**.\\n _Note: the Gemini free tier has low per-model rate limits (per minute and per day). If a cell prints a`429`/`503` agent error, wait a moment and re-run it, temporarily switch the examples to a lighter model such as `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, or use an API key with billing enabled._\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport os\\n///# Get keys for your project from the project settings page: https://cloud.langfuse.com\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY\\\", \\\"pk-lf-...\\\");\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY\\\", \\\"sk-lf-...\\\");\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_BASE_URL\\\", \\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com\\\"); ///# 🇪🇺 EU region\\n///# Other Langfuse data regions include 🇺🇸 US: https://us.cloud.langfuse.com, 🇯🇵 Japan: https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com and ⚕️ HIPAA: https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com\\n///# Gemini API Key (Get from Google AI Studio: https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey)\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"GOOGLE_API_KEY\\\", \\\"...\\\");\\n```\\nWith the environment variables set, we can now initialize the Langfuse client. `get_client()` initializes the Langfuse client using the credentials provided in the environment variables.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n///# Verify connection\\nif langfuse.auth_check():\\n print(\\\"Langfuse client is authenticated and ready!\\\")\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nelse:\\n print(\\\"Authentication failed. Please check your credentials and host.\\\")\\n```\\nLangfuse client is authenticated and ready!\\n## Step 3: OpenTelemetry Instrumentation\\nUse the [`GoogleADKInstrumentor`](https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference/tree/main/python/instrumentation/openinference-instrumentation-google-adk) library to wrap ADK calls and send OpenTelemetry spans to Langfuse.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom openinference.instrumentation.google_adk import GoogleADKInstrumentor\\nGoogleADKInstrumentor().instrument()\\n```\\n## Step 4: Run examples\\n### Example 1: Hello world agent with a tool call\\nThe smallest possible setup: one agent, one tool. Every tool call and model completion is captured as an OpenTelemetry span and forwarded to Langfuse.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom google.adk.agents import Agent\\nfrom google.adk.runners import Runner\\nfrom google.adk.sessions import InMemorySessionService\\nfrom google.genai import types\\ndef say_hello():\\n return {\\\"greeting\\\": \\\"Hello Langfuse 👋\\\"}\\nagent = Agent(\\n name=\\\"hello_agent\\\",\\n model=\\\"gemini-3.5-flash\\\",\\n instruction=\\\"Always greet using the say_hello tool.\\\",\\n tools=[say_hello],\\n)\\nAPP_NAME = \\\"hello_app\\\"\\nUSER_ID = \\\"demo-user\\\"\\nSESSION_ID = \\\"demo-session\\\"\\nsession_service = InMemorySessionService()\\n///# create_session is async → await it in notebooks\\nawait session_service.create_session(app_name=APP_NAME, user_id=USER_ID, session_id=SESSION_ID)\\nrunner = Runner(agent=agent, app_name=APP_NAME, session_service=session_service)\\nuser_msg = types.Content(role=\\\"user\\\", parts=[types.Part(text=\\\"hi\\\")])\\nfor event in runner.run(user_id=USER_ID, session_id=SESSION_ID, new_message=user_msg):\\n if event.is_final_response():\\n if event.content and event.content.parts:\\n print(event.content.parts[0].text)\\n elif event.error_message:\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n print(f\\\"Agent error: {event.error_message}\\\")\\n```\\nHello! Hello Langfuse 👋\\nLangfuse automatically maps the `user_id` and `session_id` you pass to `runner.run()` to the trace's **user** and **session** — you get [user](https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/users) and [session](https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/sessions) tracking without any extra code.\\n### Example 2: Named and filterable traces\\nBy default, traces are named after the ADK app (`invocation [hello_app]`). Use [`propagate_attributes`](https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation) to set a descriptive trace name, tags, and metadata so you can filter traces in Langfuse.\\nOne thing to watch out for: the synchronous `runner.run()` executes the agent on a background worker thread, so OpenTelemetry context — and with it everything set via `propagate_attributes` — does not reach the ADK spans. Use the async `runner.run_async()` API instead, which runs in the current context:\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import propagate_attributes\\nSESSION_ID_2 = \\\"demo-session-2\\\"\\nawait session_service.create_session(app_name=APP_NAME, user_id=USER_ID, session_id=SESSION_ID_2)\\nwith propagate_attributes(\\n trace_name=\\\"hello-agent-request\\\",\\n tags=[\\\"google-adk\\\", \\\"cookbook\\\"],\\n metadata={\\\"example\\\": \\\"named-trace\\\"},\\n):\\n async for event in runner.run_async(user_id=USER_ID, session_id=SESSION_ID_2, new_message=user_msg):\\n if event.is_final_response():\\n if event.content and event.content.parts:\\n print(event.content.parts[0].text)\\n elif event.error_message:\\n print(f\\\"Agent error: {event.error_message}\\\")\\n```\\nHello Langfuse 👋\\n### Example 3: Multi-agent pipeline with Workflow\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nReal ADK applications are rarely a single agent. ADK 2.x composes agents (and plain functions or tools) into an execution graph with [`Workflow`](https://adk.dev/workflows/) — and the trace shows every node as its own span, with its own model calls, token usage, and cost.\\nHere a `researcher` agent stores its result in session state via `output_key`, and a `writer` agent reads it through the `{research_notes}` placeholder in its instruction. The edge chain `(\\\"START\\\", researcher, writer)` runs them sequentially:\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom google.adk.workflow import Workflow\\nresearcher = Agent(\\n name=\\\"researcher\\\",\\n model=\\\"gemini-3.5-flash\\\",\\n instruction=\\\"Gather two short facts about the topic. Reply in two bullet points.\\\",\\n output_key=\\\"research_notes\\\", ///# stores the reply in session state\\n)\\nwriter = Agent(\\n name=\\\"writer\\\",\\n model=\\\"gemini-3.5-flash\\\",\\n instruction=\\\"Write a single friendly sentence summarizing: {research_notes}\\\",\\n)\\npipeline = Workflow(name=\\\"research_pipeline\\\", edges=[(\\\"START\\\", researcher, writer)])\\nPIPELINE_SESSION_ID = \\\"pipeline-session\\\"\\nawait session_service.create_session(app_name=APP_NAME, user_id=USER_ID, session_id=PIPELINE_SESSION_ID)\\npipeline_runner = Runner(agent=pipeline, app_name=APP_NAME, session_service=session_service)\\ntopic = types.Content(role=\\\"user\\\", parts=[types.Part(text=\\\"The Langfuse platform\\\")])\\nwith propagate_attributes(trace_name=\\\"research-pipeline\\\", tags=[\\\"google-adk\\\", \\\"multi-agent\\\"]):\\n async for event in pipeline_runner.run_async(user_id=USER_ID, session_id=PIPELINE_SESSION_ID, new_message=topic):\\n if event.is_final_response() and event.content and event.content.parts:\\n print(f\\\"[{event.author}]\\\", event.content.parts[0].text)\\n```\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n[researcher] * Langfuse is an open-source LLM (Large Language Model) engineering platform designed for tracing, debugging, and monitoring AI applications.\\n * It provides features for prompt management, tracking API costs and latency, and evaluating the quality of LLM outputs using both automated and manual methods. [writer] Langfuse is a wonderful open-source LLM engineering platform that helps you easily monitor, debug, and optimize your AI applications by tracking costs, managing prompts, and evaluating output quality all in one place!\\nThe trace now contains one `agent_run` span per pipeline stage, each with its own generation.\\nFor dynamic delegation, LLM agents can alternatively coordinate `sub_agents` themselves — the spans nest the same way.\\n### Example 4: Score traces with user feedback\\n[Scores](https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/scores-via-sdk) attach evaluations — user feedback, guardrail results, eval outcomes — to a trace. To score an ADK run, create the trace ID upfront, run the agent inside an enclosing Langfuse span that uses this trace ID, and pass the same ID to `create_score`:\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import Langfuse\\npredefined_trace_id = Langfuse.create_trace_id()\\nSCORED_SESSION_ID = \\\"scored-session\\\"\\nawait session_service.create_session(app_name=APP_NAME, user_id=USER_ID, session_id=SCORED_SESSION_ID)\\nfinal_response = None\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(\\n as_type=\\\"span\\\",\\n name=\\\"adk-request\\\",\\n trace_context={\\\"trace_id\\\": predefined_trace_id},\\n) as span:\\n span.update(input=\\\"hi\\\")\\n async for event in runner.run_async(user_id=USER_ID, session_id=SCORED_SESSION_ID, new_message=user_msg):\\n if event.is_final_response() and event.content and event.content.parts:\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n final_response = event.content.parts[0].text\\n print(final_response)\\n span.update(output=final_response)\\n///# e.g. triggered by a thumbs-up in your application\\nif final_response is not None:\\n langfuse.create_score(\\n trace_id=predefined_trace_id,\\n name=\\\"user-feedback\\\",\\n value=1,\\n data_type=\\\"NUMERIC\\\",\\n comment=\\\"The answer was helpful.\\\",\\n )\\n```\\nHello Langfuse 👋\\n## Step 5: View the traces in Langfuse\\nHead over to your **Langfuse dashboard → Traces**. Example 1 produces a trace with the agent loop and the tool call; Examples 2–4 add trace names, tags, nested sub-agents, and a `user-feedback` score. Traces are filterable by the users, sessions, and tags set above.\\n[Link to a public example trace in Langfuse](https://cloud.langfuse.com/project/cloramnkj0002jz088vzn1ja4/traces/fdd35393ced5a5be64ce8b8a947aef24?timestamp=2026-07-23T09%3A47%3A56.387Z&display=details)\\n## Interoperability with the Python SDK\\nYou can use this integration together with the Langfuse [SDKs](/docs/observability/sdk/overview) to add additional attributes to the observation.\\nDecoratorContext Manager\\nThe [`@observe()` decorator](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#custom-instrumentation) provides a convenient way to automatically wrap your instrumented code and add additional attributes to the observation.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import observe, propagate_attributes, get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n@observe()\\ndef my_llm_pipeline(input):\\n # Add additional attributes (user_id, session_id, metadata, version, tags) to all spans created within this execution scope\\n with propagate_attributes(\\n user_id=\\\"user_123\\\",\\n session_id=\\\"session_abc\\\",\\n tags=[\\\"agent\\\", \\\"my-observation\\\"],\\n metadata={\\\"email\\\": \\\"user@langfuse.com\\\"},\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n version=\\\"1.0.0\\\"\\n ):\\n # YOUR APPLICATION CODE HERE\\n result = call_llm(input)\\n return result\\n///# Run the function\\nmy_llm_pipeline(\\\"Hi\\\")\\n```\\nLearn more about using the Decorator in the [Langfuse SDK instrumentation docs](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#custom-instrumentation).\\nThe [Context Manager](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#custom-instrumentation) allows you to wrap your instrumented code using context managers (with `with` statements), which allows you to add additional attributes to the observation.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client, propagate_attributes\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(\\n as_type=\\\"span\\\",\\n name=\\\"my-observation\\\",\\n trace_context={\\\"trace_id\\\": \\\"abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890\\\"}, ///# Must be 32 hex chars\\n) as observation:\\n # Add additional attributes (user_id, session_id, metadata, version, tags)\\n # to all observations created within this execution scope\\n with propagate_attributes(\\n user_id=\\\"user_123\\\",\\n session_id=\\\"session_abc\\\",\\n metadata={\\\"experiment\\\": \\\"variant_a\\\", \\\"env\\\": \\\"prod\\\"},\\n version=\\\"1.0\\\",\\n ):\\n # YOUR APPLICATION CODE HERE\\n result = call_llm(\\\"some input\\\")\\n///# Flush events in short-lived applications\\nlangfuse.flush()\\n```\\nLearn more about using the Context Manager in the [Langfuse SDK instrumentation docs](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#custom-instrumentation).\\n## Troubleshooting\\nNo observations appearing\\nFirst, enable [debug mode](/docs/observability/sdk/advanced-features#logging--debugging) in the Python SDK:\\n \\n \\n```\\nexport LANGFUSE_DEBUG=\\\"True\\\"\\n```\\nThen run your application and check the debug logs:\\n * **OTel observations appear in the logs:** Your application is instrumented correctly but observations are not reaching Langfuse. To resolve this: \"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"1. Call [`langfuse.flush()`](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#client-lifecycle--flushing) at the end of your application to ensure all observations are exported.\\n 2. Verify that you are using the correct API keys and base URL.\\n * **No OTel spans in the logs:** Your application is not instrumented correctly. Make sure the instrumentation runs before your application code.\\nUnwanted observations in Langfuse\\nThe Langfuse SDK is based on OpenTelemetry. Other libraries in your application may emit OTel spans that are not relevant to you. These still count toward your [billable units](/docs/administration/billable-units), so you should filter them out. See [Unwanted spans in Langfuse](/faq/all/unwanted-http-database-spans) for details.\\nMissing attributes\\nSome attributes may be stored in the metadata object of the observation rather than being mapped to the Langfuse data model. If a mapping or integration does not work as expected, please [raise an issue on GitHub](/issues).\\n## Next Steps\\nOnce you have instrumented your code, you can manage, evaluate and debug your application:\\n[\\n### Manage prompts in Langfuse\\n](/docs/prompts/get-started)\\n[\\n### Add evaluation scores\\n](/docs/evaluation/features/evaluation-methods/custom-scores)\\n[\\n### Run LLM-as-a-judge Evaluators\\n](/docs/scores/model-based-evals)\\n[\\n### Create datasets\\n](/docs/datasets/overview)\\n[\\n### Create custom dashboards\\n](/docs/analytics/custom-dashboards)\\n[\\n### Test queries in the Playground\\n](/docs/playground)\\n* * *\\n* * *\\nLast edited 8/4/2026\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview\", \"title\": \"Observability & Application Tracing\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"LLM Observability & Application Tracing (Open Source) - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Observability](/docs/observability/overview)\\n[Overview](/docs/observability/overview)\\n# Observability & Application Tracing\\nGenerative AI systems are inherently non-deterministic. Therefore, debugging your application without any observability tool is more like guesswork. Implementing comprehensive AI observability gives you the tools to understand what's happening inside your application and why. It is the foundation for continuously evaluating and improving your system.\\nThe core of this is **application tracing** — structured logs of every request that capture the exact prompt sent, the model's response, token usage, latency, and any tools or retrieval steps in between.\\nHere's an example of a trace in the Langfuse UI:\\n🚀\\nWant to see it in action? [**Create a free account**](/cloud) and explore Langfuse Observability in the [interactive example project](/docs/demo).\\n## Getting Started\\nStart by [setting up your first trace](/docs/observability/get-started), and compare it against our [best practices guide](/docs/observability/best-practices) so you're set up for success. If you're new to AI observability, take a look at the [core concepts](/docs/observability/data-model) too.\\n## Use your traces\\nOnce traces are coming in, the next step is to make sense of them and use what you learn to improve your agent. Read the chapter on [Monitoring in the Langfuse Academy](/academy/monitoring) to learn how to utilize your traces well.\\nFor feature-specific implementation guidance, these are the most common ones to start with:\\n * Track [model usage and cost](/docs/observability/features/token-and-cost-tracking)\\n * Monitor application quality with [scores](/docs/evaluation/scores/overview)\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n * Analyze cost, latency, volume, and quality in [custom dashboards](/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards)\\n * Get notified when a metric crosses a threshold with [alerts](/docs/observability/features/alerts)\\nBrowse the Features section in the sidebar for a complete list of observability features.\\n## FAQ\\nWhat is the difference between observability and tracing?\\n+\\n **Observability** is the broader capability of understanding the internal state of your system from its outputs. It encompasses tracing, metrics, and logging. **Tracing** is a specific observability technique that records the flow of a request through your system, preserving causal relationships between operations. In the context of LLM applications, tracing is the most important observability tool because it captures the full context of each request — prompts, responses, tool calls, and their relationships.\\nWhat is application tracing?\\n+\\nApplication tracing records the complete lifecycle of a request as it flows through your system. Each trace captures every operation — LLM calls, retrieval steps, tool executions, and custom logic — along with timing, inputs, outputs, and metadata. This gives you full visibility into what happened during each request, enabling debugging, performance optimization, and quality monitoring.\\nHow does Langfuse compare to other tracing solutions?\\n+\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nLangfuse is purpose-built for LLM applications, which means it natively understands LLM-specific concepts like token usage, model parameters, prompt/completion pairs, and evaluation scores. Unlike general-purpose APM tools, Langfuse provides features specific to AI engineering: [LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/llm-as-a-judge), [prompt management](/docs/prompt-management/overview), [experiments and datasets](/docs/evaluation/experiments/datasets), and [custom dashboards](/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards). It's also [open source](/self-hosting) and can be self-hosted.\\nDoes Langfuse add latency to my application?\\n+\\nNo. Langfuse SDKs send tracing data asynchronously in the background. Trace events are queued locally and flushed in batches, so your application's response time is not affected. See [queuing and batching](/docs/observability/features/queuing-batching) for details.\\n* * *\\n* * *\\nLast edited 8/28/2026\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"site\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/resources/engineering/langfuse-vs-datadog\", \"title\": \"Langfuse vs. Datadog for LLM Observability & Agent Tracing - Langfuse\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"**OpenTelemetry**| OTel-native SDKs + OTLP endpoint| OTLP ingestion (GenAI semantic conventions 1.37+) \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**First-party SDKs**| Python, JS/TS (OTel-native); other languages via OTel| Python, Node.js, Java \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**Entry price**| Free (50k units/mo); Core $29/mo| Free (40k LLM spans/mo); Pro $160/mo billed annually \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n## Open Source & Distribution\\n\\n---\\n\\nLangfuse is open source (MIT) and [self-hosting](/self-hosting) is a first-class deployment option with the same codebase as Langfuse Cloud. Datadog is a proprietary SaaS platform; its products, including LLM Observability, run on Datadog-hosted regional sites and store data on Datadog's infrastructure ([source](https://docs.datadoghq.com/getting_started/site/), checked 2026-07).\\n\\n---\\n\\nFeature| Langfuse| Datadog \\n---|---|--- \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**Model**| **[Open Source](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse)** (MIT License)| **Proprietary SaaS** (Closed Source) \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**GitHub Stars**| [](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse)| N/A \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**Self-Hosting**| **First-Class Citizen** : Docker Compose, Kubernetes (Helm), and Terraform templates for AWS, Azure, and GCP.| **Not available** : The platform runs only as Datadog-hosted SaaS (the Datadog Agent runs locally, data does not stay local). \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**Data Sovereignty**| **High** : Can run fully air-gapped in your own VPC or on-premises.| **Regional choice** : Nine hosted sites (US, EU, Japan, Australia, UK, US-gov); data resides with Datadog. \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\nIf self-hosting or air-gapped deployment is a hard requirement, this section already decides the comparison: Datadog does not offer a self-hosted platform (checked 2026-07).\\n## LLM & Agent Tracing\\n\\n---\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Both platforms capture hierarchical traces of LLM applications and agents, including token usage, latency, errors, and cost. The difference is scope and surrounding context: Langfuse is [purpose-built for LLM observability](/docs/observability/overview) and covers 100+ frameworks and model providers, while Datadog embeds LLM traces into its general observability platform and correlates them with APM services, logs, and real user sessions.\\n\\n---\\n\\nFeature| Langfuse| Datadog \\n---|---|--- \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**SDKs**| **Python and JS/TS** , built natively on OpenTelemetry.| **Python, Node.js, and Java** , with automatic and manual instrumentation ([source](https://docs.datadoghq.com/llm_observability/instrumentation/sdk/)). \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**Auto-instrumentation**| 100+ integrations, including OpenAI, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Vercel AI SDK, LiteLLM, CrewAI.| Integrations include OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, AWS Bedrock, Gemini, Vertex AI, CrewAI, and Strands Agents. \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**Other languages**| Java, Go, and any OTel-capable stack via the OTLP endpoint.| HTTP API for non-SDK languages. \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**Platform context**| Sessions, users, environments, releases, agent graph views.| Correlation with Datadog APM, infrastructure metrics, logs, and RUM sessions. \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n## Evaluation\\n\\n---\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Both platforms ship a working evaluation loop; the implementations differ in where evaluations run and how far they extend. [Langfuse evaluations](/docs/evaluation/overview) include managed LLM-as-a-judge evaluators, code-based evaluators, custom scores via SDK/API, human annotation queues, and dataset experiments, all of which also run in self-hosted deployments. Datadog provides LLM-as-a-judge templates (including Hallucination, Failure to Answer, Toxicity and Prompt Injection), custom LLM-as-a-judge evaluators defined in natural language, external evaluations submitted via API, and annotation queues ([source](https://docs.datadoghq.com/llm_observability/evaluations/), checked 2026-07).\\n\\n---\\n\\nFeature| Langfuse| Datadog \\n---|---|--- \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**LLM-as-a-judge**| Managed evaluators on any traced data, incl. tool-call evaluators.| Template and custom judge evaluators. \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**Code-based evaluators**| Deterministic evaluators run natively.| External via API or third-party frameworks (e.g., DeepEval). \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**Human review**| Annotation queues.| Annotation queues. \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**Datasets/experiments**| Datasets, experiments, and prompt experiments via UI, SDK, and API.| Datasets and experiments with Playground integration. \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**Where evals run**| Cloud or your own infrastructure (self-hosted).| Datadog's SaaS platform. \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n## Prompt Management\\n\\n---\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"This is the largest functional gap between the two products. [Langfuse prompt management](/docs/prompt-management/overview) is a runtime system: prompts are versioned in Langfuse, deployed via release labels, fetched by your application through cached SDK calls, and linked to the traces and evaluation scores they produce. Prompt fetching is unlimited on all plans, including the free tier.\\n\\n---\\n\\nDatadog offers Prompt Tracking, which links prompt templates and versions that are defined in your code to LLM spans for version history, diffs, and trace filtering. Applications do not fetch prompts from Datadog at runtime; it is an observability feature, not a prompt deployment system ([source](https://docs.datadoghq.com/llm_observability/monitoring/prompt_tracking/), checked 2026-07).\\n\\n---\\n\\nIf you want to update or roll back prompts without a code deploy, run A/B tests across prompt versions, or hand prompt iteration to non-engineers, Langfuse covers that workflow and Datadog does not.\\n## Pricing\\n\\n---\\n\\nThe billing models are structurally different, so read the units carefully before comparing numbers. Langfuse bills [units](/docs/administration/billable-units), where one unit is a trace, an observation, or a score. Datadog bills only LLM inference spans; tool, workflow, agent, embedding, and retrieval spans are free ([source](https://www.datadoghq.com/pricing/list/), checked 2026-07). A single agent request can therefore produce a different billable count on each platform, and the fairest comparison is to model your own traffic on both.\\n\\n---\\n\\nFeature| Langfuse| Datadog LLM Observability \\n---|---|--- \\n \\n\\n---\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n**Free tier**| 50k units/mo, 30 days data access. Self-hosted OSS: unlimited, free (MIT).| 40k LLM spans/mo, 15-day retention, full feature access. \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**Paid entry**| **Core: $29/mo** (100k units included).| **Pro: $160/mo billed annually** ($200 month-to-month) for the first 100k LLM spans. \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**Additional usage**| $8 per 100k units, decreasing to $6 per 100k at volume.| $3.50 per 10k additional LLM spans (annual billing). \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**Retention**| Core: 90 days. Pro ($199/mo): 3 years.| 15 days included; extensions to 30/60/90 days cost $1.50/$3.00/$4.00 per 10k spans. \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\n**Enterprise**| [$2,499/mo](/pricing), incl. audit logs, SCIM, SLAs.| Custom, typically part of a broader Datadog agreement. \\n \\n\\n---\\n\\nTwo practical notes. First, Datadog's free and Pro tiers include full feature access, which is a low barrier for teams already inside the Datadog ecosystem. Second, Datadog's 15-day default retention is short for LLM engineering workflows like building evaluation datasets from historical production traces; extended retention is a paid add-on, while Langfuse Core includes 90 days and Pro includes 3 years.\\n## Using Langfuse and Datadog Together\\n\\n---\\n\\nChoosing Langfuse rarely means dropping Datadog. The most common production setup we see keeps Datadog for application and infrastructure monitoring and adds Langfuse for LLM engineering: deep trace inspection, evaluations, prompt management, and dataset curation. Because the [Langfuse SDKs are OTel-native](/integrations/native/opentelemetry), both backends can be fed from one instrumentation layer by attaching two span processors to a shared `TracerProvider`:\\n\\n---\\n\\n \\n \\n```\\n\\n\\nfrom opentelemetry import trace\\n\\n\\nfrom opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider\\n\\n\\nfrom opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor\\n\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nfrom opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.http.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter\\n\\n\\nfrom langfuse.opentelemetry import LangfuseSpanProcessor\\n\\n\\nprovider = TracerProvider()\\n\\n\\n///# Langfuse receives LLM and GenAI spans (default filter)\\nprovider.add_span_processor(LangfuseSpanProcessor())\\n///# Datadog (or any APM) receives everything via your existing OTLP endpoint\\nprovider.add_span_processor(\\n\\n\\n BatchSpanProcessor(OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint=\\\"http://localhost:4318/v1/traces\\\"))\\n\\n\\n)\\ntrace.set_tracer_provider(provider)\\n\\n\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\nThe Langfuse span processor filters for LLM-relevant spans by default, so your APM keeps the full application picture while Langfuse stays focused on the GenAI layer. Datadog also accepts OpenTelemetry GenAI spans directly (semantic conventions 1.37+ over OTLP), so a collector-based fan-out to both backends works as well. Configuration details, isolated-provider setups, and troubleshooting for this pattern are covered in [using Langfuse with an existing OpenTelemetry setup](/faq/all/existing-otel-setup).\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Is Langfuse an alternative to Datadog LLM Observability?\\nYes, for the LLM application layer. Langfuse covers tracing, evaluations, prompt management, and datasets/experiments, and adds self-hosting and an MIT open-source license that Datadog does not offer. Langfuse is not an APM, so it complements rather than replaces Datadog's infrastructure and application monitoring.\\n### Can I self-host Datadog LLM Observability?\\n\\n---\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nNo. Datadog runs as a hosted SaaS across nine regional sites, and telemetry data is stored on Datadog's infrastructure (checked July 2026). Langfuse is open source (MIT) and can be [self-hosted](/self-hosting) with Docker Compose, Kubernetes, or Terraform templates, including air-gapped deployments.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### How much does Datadog LLM Observability cost?\\nAs of July 2026, Datadog offers a free tier with 40k LLM spans per month and 15-day retention, and a Pro plan at $160/month (billed annually) covering the first 100k LLM spans, with additional spans at $3.50 per 10k. Only LLM inference spans are billed; tool, workflow, and retrieval spans are free. Extended retention to 30, 60, or 90 days is a paid add-on.\\n### Can I use Langfuse and Datadog at the same time?\\nYes, and this is a common setup. Both products consume OpenTelemetry traces, so one instrumentation layer can feed Datadog for APM and Langfuse for LLM engineering, either via two span processors in your application or a collector-based fan-out. See [using Langfuse with an existing OpenTelemetry setup](/faq/all/existing-otel-setup) for working configurations.\\n\\n---\\n\\nThis comparison is out of date? Please [raise a pull request](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/tree/main/content/resources/engineering) with up-to-date information.\\n\\n---\\n\\nLast edited 7/15/2026\\n\\n---\\n\\n[Braintrust Data Alternatives? The best LLMOps platform?](/resources/engineering/best-braintrustdata-alternatives)\\n[How to Migrate from Helicone to Langfuse](/resources/engineering/migrate-from-helicone)\\n\\n---\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nLangfuse vs. DatadogLangfuse and Datadog at a GlanceOpen Source & DistributionLLM & Agent TracingEvaluationPrompt ManagementPricingUsing Langfuse and Datadog TogetherIs Langfuse an alternative to Datadog LLM Observability?Can I self-host Datadog LLM Observability?How much does Datadog LLM Observability cost?Can I use Langfuse and Datadog at the same time?\\n[Give us feedback](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/issues/new?title=Feedback+for+%22Langfuse+vs.+Datadog+for+LLM+Observability+%26+Agent+Tracing%22&labels=feedback)\\n[Edit this page on GitHub](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/edit/main/content/resources/engineering/langfuse-vs-datadog.mdx)\\nLast edited Jul 15, 2026\\n\\n---\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"site\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/press\", \"title\": \"Press & Media - Langfuse\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"---\\n\\n[Langfuse joins ClickHouse! →Langfuse joins ClickHouse! Learn more →](/blog/joining-clickhouse)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[Hiring in Berlin and SFLooking for GOATS!](/careers)\\n[Changelog](/changelog)\\n[21K](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse \\\"GitHub Repository\\\")\\n[Get Demo](/talk-to-us)\\n\\n---\\n\\n# Press & Media\\n\\n---\\n\\nWant to talk about press opportunities? Email [clemens@langfuse.com](mailto:clemens@langfuse.com) and we’ll be in touch shortly. To keep in touch with Langfuse, follow us on [Twitter](https://x.com/langfuse), [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/company/langfuse), [GitHub](https://github.com/langfuse), and [Discord](https://langfuse.com/discord).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Company Facts\\n\\n---\\n\\nLangfuse is building the open source LLM engineering platform to help teams build production-grade LLM applications faster. The platform provides:\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Observability & Tracing** — Production tracing, metrics, and analytics for LLM applications\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Prompt Management** — Version control and deployment of prompts with integrated monitoring\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Evaluations** — LLM-as-a-Judge evaluations, datasets, and structured evaluation processes\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Collaboration** — Shareable views, dashboards, and team collaboration features\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Company\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Founded:** 2023\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Headquarters:** Berlin, Germany (Product & Engineering) and San Francisco, CA (Marketing & Sales)\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Team Size:** 14+ full-time employees\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Y Combinator:** Winter 2023 batch (W23)\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Public Company Handbook:** [langfuse.com/handbook](/handbook/chapters/story)\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Funding\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **$4M Seed Round** (November 2023)\\n * **Investors:** Lightspeed Venture Partners, General Catalyst (La Famiglia), Y Combinator, plus angels and operators in ML, Open Source, and Developer Tools\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Most Important Links\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **[Video Demo](/watch-demo)**\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Company Handbook:** [langfuse.com/handbook](/handbook/chapters/story)\\n\\n---\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n * **Changelog:** [langfuse.com/changelog](/changelog)\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Enterprise:** [langfuse.com/enterprise](/enterprise)\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Documentation:** [langfuse.com/docs](/docs)\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Roadmap:** [langfuse.com/docs/roadmap](/docs/roadmap)\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Blog:** [langfuse.com/blog](/blog)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Why does Langfuse exist?\\n\\n---\\n\\nLangfuse exists to accelerate the deployment of reliable, safe, explainable and cost-effective AI applications and agents.\\nAI will create meaningful value for society and drive economic growth and we are still in the early days of seeing this impact. Over time, every successful company will be an AI company, with AI at the core of its strategy, value creation, and business processes. Most value creation will happen at the application-layer, split between incumbents and AI-native startups.\\n\\n---\\n\\nWe’re building an [integrated](/integrations) and [open](/handbook/chapters/open-source) tooling layer to help teams with:\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Visibility & explainability** → _Langfuse Observability_ (production tracing, metrics, and analytics)\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Collaboration across disciplines** → _Prompt management, shareable views & dashboards_\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Evaluation & data operations** → _Langfuse Evaluations (evals,
