Langfuse\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"---\\n\\n[](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse \\\"GitHub Repository\\\")\\n\\n---\\n\\n * [Overview](/security)\\n\\n---\\n\\n * Compliance\\n * Privacy\\n * Contact\\n * General Information on Langfuse\\n * What is Langfuse?\\n * What deployment models are available?\\n * Which cloud provider and regions do you use?\\n[Question? Give us feedback →](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/issues/new?title=Feedback%20for%20%E2%80%9CSecurity%20%26%20Compliance%20Overview%E2%80%9D&labels=feedback)\\n[Edit this page on GitHub](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/tree/main/pages/security/index.mdx)\\n[Akio NuernbergerEnterprise & Partnerships](https://twitter.com/AkioNuernberger)\\n\\n---\\n\\nSecurity & ComplianceOverview\\n\\n---\\n\\n# Security & Compliance Overview\\n\\n---\\n\\n**At Langfuse, we prioritize data privacy and security.** We understand that the data you entrust to us is a vital asset to your business, and we treat it with the utmost care.\\n\\n---\\n\\nWe take active steps to demonstrate our commitment to data security and privacy such as annual SOC2 Type 2 and ISO27001 audits as well as External Penetration Tests. You can request access to the reports [here](/request-security-docs).\\n\\n---\\n\\nLangfuse is built with enterprise needs in mind, focusing on:\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Security Measures:** Robust [Encryption](/security/encryption), access controls, and regular [Penetration Testing](/security/penetration-testing).\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Privacy Measures:** Protecting user data according to regulations like [GDPR](/security/gdpr). We offer a [DPA](/security/dpa), [BAA](/security/hipaa), and adhere to our [Privacy Policy](/privacy).\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Transparency:** Open-source core and clear information on [software dependencies](/security/dependencies).\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Reporting:** Clear channels for [Responsible Disclosure](/security/responsible-disclosure) and [Whistleblowing](/security/whistleblowing).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Compliance\\n\\n---\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nWe maintain [internal policies](/security/policies) and adhere to several industry-standard compliance frameworks. Please check [Security FAQs](/security/security-faq) for more details.\\n\\n---\\n\\n[SOC 2 Type II](/security/soc2)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[ISO 27001](/security/iso27001)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[HIPAA](/security/hipaa)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Privacy\\n\\n---\\n\\nLangfuse is [GDPR](/security/gdpr) compliant, and offers data retention, data masking and data deletion capabilities to [manage the processing of personal data](/security/manage-personal-data). You can enter into a [DPA](/security/dpa) with Langfuse.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Contact\\n\\n---\\n\\n * Use [Ask AI](/ask-ai) to get instant answers to your questions.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * For security inquiries: [security@langfuse.com](mailto:security@langfuse.com)\\n\\n---\\n\\n * For privacy inquiries: [privacy@langfuse.com](mailto:privacy@langfuse.com)\\n\\n---\\n\\n * For compliance inquiries: [compliance@langfuse.com](mailto:compliance@langfuse.com)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## General Information on Langfuse\\n\\n---\\n\\n### What is Langfuse?\\n\\n---\\n\\nLangfuse is an **open‑source LLM engineering platform** that provides tracing, prompt management, evaluation, and metrics to help teams debug and continuously improve LLM‑based applications.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### What deployment models are available?\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Langfuse Cloud** – fully‑managed SaaS (multi‑tenant) with US, EU and HIPAA data regions\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Self‑hosted OSS** – MIT‑licensed software that you can deploy on your own infrastructure\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Self‑hosted Enterprise Edition** – commercial license with additional security/compliance features and vendor support.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Which cloud provider and regions do you use?\\n\\n---\\n\\nLangfuse Cloud mainly runs on **AWS and Clickhouse via AWS** :\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **US region** : us-west-2 (Oregon)\\n * **EU region** : eu-west-1 (Ireland)\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"site\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/resources/engineering/migrate-from-phoenix\", \"title\": \"Migrate from Arize Phoenix to Langfuse - Langfuse\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nOTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS=\\\"Authorization=Basic ${AUTH_STRING},x-langfuse-ingestion-version=4\\\"\\n\\n\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n`AUTH_STRING` is your base64-encoded Langfuse project keys (`echo -n \\\"pk-lf-...:sk-lf-...\\\" | base64`). If your exporter requires signal-specific configuration, the traces path is `/api/public/otel/v1/traces`. Langfuse accepts OTLP over HTTP in both protobuf and JSON encodings (no gRPC).\\n\\n---\\n\\nFramework auto-instrumentation (LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI SDK, and the other OpenInference instrumentations) keeps working unchanged: the spans simply arrive in Langfuse, where GenAI/OpenInference attributes map to Langfuse generations, tool observations, token usage, and cost tracking.\\nTwo things to verify in the first hour:\\n\\n---\\n\\n 1. **Trace grouping** : check that multi-span requests arrive as one trace with the expected hierarchy (see [OTel property mapping](/integrations/native/opentelemetry) if attributes land differently than expected).\\n 2. **User/session attribution** : Langfuse reads `user.id` and `session.id` attributes; populate them where you previously relied on Phoenix-specific metadata.\\n\\n---\\n\\nYou can also run both backends in parallel during a validation window by configuring an OTel collector with two exporters, a common pattern for de-risking the cutover.\\n## Step 2: Migrate datasets\\nExport dataset examples from Phoenix (via its API/SDK) and recreate them with the Langfuse SDK. The shapes are close: each example's input, expected output, and metadata map directly:\\n\\n---\\n\\n \\n \\n```\\n\\n\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\n\\n\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n\\n\\nfor example in phoenix_examples: ///# from Phoenix's dataset export\\n\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/integrations/other/mlflow\", \"title\": \"MLflow Integration via OpenTelemetry\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"MLflow Integration via OpenTelemetry - Langfuse\\n[Integrations](/integrations)\\n[Other](/integrations/other/agentic-data-stack)\\n[MLflow](/integrations/other/mlflow)\\nThis is a Jupyter notebook\\n[Open on GitHub](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/blob/main/cookbook/otel_integration_mlflow.ipynb)\\n[Run on Google Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/langfuse/langfuse-docs/blob/main/cookbook/otel_integration_mlflow.ipynb)\\n# MLflow Integration via OpenTelemetry\\nLangfuse is an [OpenTelemetry backend](https://langfuse.com/docs/opentelemetry/get-started), allowing trace ingestion from various OpenTelemetry instrumentation libraries. This guide demonstrates how to use the [MLflow](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/tracing/integrations/) instrumentation library to instrument a compatible framework or LLM provider.\\n## Step 1: Install Dependencies\\nInstall the necessary Python packages: `openai`, `langfuse`, and `mlflow`. These will allow you to interact with OpenAI as well as setup the instrumentation for tracing.\\n \\n \\n```\\n%pip install mlflow openai opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http langfuse --upgrade\\n```\\n## Step 2: Configure Environment Variables\\nBefore sending any requests, you need to configure your credentials and endpoints. First, set up the Langfuse authentication by providing your public and secret keys. Then, configure the OpenTelemetry exporter endpoint and headers to point to Langfuse's backend. You should also specify your OpenAI API key.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport os\\nimport base64\\nLANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY = \\\"pk-lf-...\\\"\\nLANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY = \\\"sk-lf-...\\\"\\nLANGFUSE_AUTH = base64.b64encode(f\\\"{LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}:{LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\\\".encode()).decode()\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT\\\", \\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel/v1/traces\\\"); ///# 🇪🇺 EU data region\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/core-concepts\", \"title\": \"Core Concepts\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Concepts - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Evaluation](/docs/evaluation/overview)\\n[Concepts](/docs/evaluation/core-concepts)\\n# Core Concepts\\nThis page digs into the different concepts of evaluations, and what's available in Langfuse.\\nIf you are still deciding _what_ to measure, [Choosing what to evaluate in the Langfuse Academy](/academy/evaluate/choosing-what-to-evaluate) works through how to turn observed failures into a small set of metrics, and [Writing good evaluators](/academy/evaluate/writing-evaluators) covers how to make those checks trustworthy.\\nReady to start?\\n * [Create a dataset](/docs/evaluation/experiments/datasets) to measure your LLM application's performance consistently\\n * [Run an experiment](/docs/evaluation/core-concepts#experiments) to get an overview of how your application is doing\\n * [Set up LLM-as-a-Judge](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/llm-as-a-judge) to evaluate your live traces\\n * [Create a code evaluator](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/code-evaluators) for deterministic checks\\n## The Evaluation Loop\\nLLM applications often have a constant [loop of testing and monitoring](/academy/ai-engineering-loop).\\n**[Offline evaluation](/academy/evaluate)** lets you test your application against a fixed dataset before you deploy. You run your new prompt or model against test cases, review the scores, iterate until the results look good, then deploy your changes. In Langfuse, you can do that by running [Experiments](/docs/evaluation/core-concepts#experiments).\\n**[Online evaluation](/academy/monitoring)** scores live traces to catch issues in real traffic. When you find edge cases your dataset didn't cover, you add them back to your dataset so future experiments will catch them.\\nDeploy\\n[OnlineTracetraces · sessions · agents · prompts](/academy/tracing)\\n[OnlineMonitordashboards · LLM-as-judge · feedback](/academy/monitoring)\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n[OfflineBuild datasetsdatasets · features-as-tests](/academy/datasets)\\n[OfflineExperimentprompts · models · code variants](/academy/experiments)\\n[OfflineEvaluatejudges · custom evals · annotation](/academy/evaluate)\\n> **Here's an example workflow** for building a customer support chatbot\\n> \\n> 1. You update your prompt to make responses less formal.\\n> 2. Before deploying, you run an **experiment** : test the new prompt against your dataset of customer questions **(offline evaluation)**.\\n> 3. You review the scores and outputs. The tone improved, but responses are longer and some miss important links.\\n> 4. You refine the prompt and run the experiment again.\\n> 5. The results look good now. You deploy the new prompt to production.\\n> 6. You monitor with **online evaluation** to catch any new edge cases.\\n> 7. You notice that a customer asked a question in French, but the bot responded in English.\\n> 8. You add this French query to your dataset so future experiments will catch this issue.\\n> 9. You update your prompt to support French responses and run another experiment.\\n> \\n> \\n> Over time, your dataset grows from a couple of examples to a diverse, representative set of real-world test cases.\\n## Scores\\n[Scores](/docs/evaluation/scores/overview) are Langfuse's universal data object for storing evaluation results. Any time you want to assign a quality judgment to an LLM output, whether by a human annotation, an LLM judge, a programmatic check, or end-user feedback, the result is stored as a score.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nScores can be attached to traces, observations, sessions, or dataset runs. Every score has a **name** , a **value** , and a **data type** (`NUMERIC`, `CATEGORICAL`, `BOOLEAN`, or `TEXT`). Learn more about [score types](/docs/evaluation/scores/overview#score-types), [how to create scores](/docs/evaluation/scores/overview#how-to-create-scores), and [score analytics](/docs/evaluation/scores/score-analytics) on the dedicated [Scores](/docs/evaluation/scores/overview) page.\\n## Evaluation Methods\\nEvaluation methods are the functions that score traces, observations, sessions, or dataset runs. You can use a variety of evaluation methods to add scores.\\nMethod| What| Use when \\n---|---|--- \\n[LLM-as-a-Judge](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/llm-as-a-judge)| Use an LLM to evaluate outputs based on custom criteria| Subjective assessments at scale (tone, accuracy, helpfulness) \\n[Code evaluators](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/code-evaluators)| Run custom Python or TypeScript logic to score observations or experiments| Deterministic checks, structured output validation, custom business rules \\n[Scores via UI](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/scores-via-ui)| Manually add scores to traces directly in the Langfuse UI| Quick quality spot checks, reviewing individual traces \\n[Annotation Queues](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/annotation-queues)| Structured human review workflows with customizable queues| Building ground truth, systematic labeling, team collaboration \\n[Scores via API/SDK](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/scores-via-sdk)| Programmatically add scores using the Langfuse API or SDK| Custom evaluation pipelines, deterministic checks, automated workflows \\n \\nWhen setting up new evaluation methods, you can use [Score Analytics](/docs/evaluation/scores/score-analytics) to analyze or sense-check the scores you produce.\\n## Online evaluation\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nYou can compare experiment runs to see if a new prompt version improves scores, or identify specific inputs where your application struggles. Based on these experiment results, you can decide whether the change is ready to be deployed to production.\\nYou can find more details on how these objects link together under the hood on the [data model page](/docs/evaluation/experiments/data-model).\\n### Two ways to run experiments\\nYou can **run experiments programmatically using the Langfuse SDK**. This gives you full control over the task, evaluation logic, and more. [Learn more about running experiments via SDK](/docs/evaluation/experiments/experiments-via-sdk).\\nAnother way is to **run experiments directly from the Langfuse interface** by selecting a dataset and prompt version. This is useful for quick iterations on prompts without writing code. [Learn more about running experiments via UI](/docs/evaluation/experiments/experiments-via-ui).\\n**Langfuse Execution**\\n **Local/CI Execution**\\n **Langfuse Dataset**\\n[Experiments via UI](/docs/evaluation/experiments/experiments-via-ui)\\n[Experiments via SDK](/docs/evaluation/experiments/experiments-via-sdk)\\n **Local Dataset**\\nNot supported\\n[Experiments via SDK](/docs/evaluation/experiments/experiments-via-sdk)\\n_While it's optional, we recommend managing the underlying[Datasets](/docs/evaluation/experiments/datasets) in Langfuse as it allows for [1] In-UI comparison tables of different experiments on the same data and [2] Iteratively improve dataset based on production/staging traces._\\n* * *\\n* * *\\nLast edited 8/31/2026\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs\", \"title\": \"Langfuse Overview\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Overview - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Overview](/docs)\\n# Langfuse Overview\\nLangfuse is an open-source AI engineering platform ([GitHub](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse)) that helps teams collaboratively debug, analyze, and iterate on their AI agent applications. All platform features are natively integrated to accelerate the development workflow. Langfuse is open, self-hostable, and extensible ([ _why Langfuse?_](/why)).\\n### Observability\\n * Log traces\\n * Lowest level transparency\\n * Understand cost and latency\\n### Prompts\\n * Version control and deploy\\n * Collaborate on prompts\\n * Test prompts and models\\n### Evaluation\\n * Measure output quality\\n * Monitor production health\\n * Test changes in development\\n### Platform\\n * API-first architecture\\n * Data exports to blob storage\\n * Enterprise security and administration\\n## Observability\\n[Observability](/docs/observability/overview) is essential for understanding and debugging AI agent applications. Unlike traditional software, AI agent applications involve complex, non-deterministic interactions that can be challenging to monitor and debug. Langfuse provides comprehensive tracing capabilities that help you understand exactly what's happening in your application.\\n * Traces include all LLM and non-LLM calls, including retrieval, embedding, API calls, and more\\n * Support for tracking multi-turn conversations as sessions and user tracking\\n * Agents can be represented as graphs\\n * Capture traces via our native SDKs for Python/JS, 100+ library/framework integrations, OpenTelemetry, or via an LLM Gateway such as LiteLLM\\n * Based on OpenTelemetry to increase compatibility and reduce vendor lock-in\\n🚀\\nWant to see it in action?\\n[Create a free account](/cloud) and explore Langfuse Observability in the [interactive example project](/docs/demo).\\nTrace DetailsSessionsTimelineUsersAgent GraphsDashboardAlerts\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nTraces allow you to track every LLM call and other relevant logic in your app.\\nSessions allow you to track multi-step conversations or agentic workflows.\\nDebug latency issues by inspecting the timeline view.\\nAdd your own `userId` to monitor costs and usage for each user. Optionally, create a deep link to this view in your systems.\\nLLM agents can be visualized as a graph to illustrate the flow of complex agentic workflows.\\nSee quality, cost, and latency metrics in the dashboard to monitor your LLM application.\\nGet notified over Slack, GitHub Actions, or Webhooks when a metric crosses a threshold with [alerts](/docs/observability/features/alerts).\\n## Prompt Management\\n[Prompt Management](/docs/prompt-management/overview) is critical in building effective AI applications. Langfuse provides tools to help you manage, version, and optimize your prompts throughout the development lifecycle.\\n * [Get started](/docs/prompt-management/get-started) with prompt management\\n * Manage, version, and optimize your prompts throughout the development lifecycle\\n * Test prompts interactively in the [LLM Playground](/docs/prompt-management/features/playground)\\n * Run [Experiments](/docs/evaluation/features/prompt-experiments) against datasets to test new prompt versions directly within Langfuse\\n🚀\\nWant to see it in action? [**Create a free account**](/cloud) and explore Langfuse Prompt Management in the [interactive example project](/docs/demo).\\nCreateVersion ControlDeployMetricsTest in PlaygroundLink with TracesTrack Changes\\nCreate a new prompt via UI, SDKs, or API.\\nCollaboratively version and edit prompts via UI, API, or SDKs.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nDeploy prompts to production or any environment via labels - without any code changes.\\nCompare latency, cost, and evaluation metrics across different versions of your prompts.\\nInstantly test your prompts in the playground.\\nLink prompts with traces to understand how they perform in the context of your LLM application.\\nTrack changes to your prompts to understand how they evolve over time.\\n## Evaluation\\n[Evaluation](/docs/evaluation/overview) is crucial for ensuring the quality and reliability of your LLM applications. Langfuse provides flexible evaluation tools that adapt to your specific needs, whether you're testing in development or monitoring production performance.\\n * Get started with different [evaluation methods](/docs/evaluation/overview): LLM-as-a-judge, code evaluators, user feedback, manual labeling, or custom pipelines\\n * Identify issues early by running evaluations on production traces\\n * Create and manage [Datasets](/docs/evaluation/features/datasets) for systematic testing in development that ensure your application performs reliably across different scenarios\\n * Run [Experiments](/docs/evaluation/core-concepts#experiments) to systematically test your LLM application\\n🚀\\nWant to see it in action? [**Create a free account**](/cloud) and explore Langfuse Evaluation in the [interactive example project](/docs/demo).\\nAnalyticsUser FeedbackLLM-as-a-JudgeExperimentsAnnotation QueueCustom Evals\\nPlot evaluation results in the Langfuse Dashboard.\\nCollect feedback from your users. Can be captured in the frontend via our Browser SDK, server-side via the SDKs or API. Video includes example application.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nRun fully managed LLM-as-a-judge evaluations on production or development traces. Can be applied to any step within your application for step-wise evaluations.\\nEvaluate prompts and models on datasets directly in the user interface. No custom code is needed.\\nBaseline your evaluation workflow with human annotations via Annotation Queues.\\nAdd custom evaluation results, supports numeric, boolean and categorical values.\\n \\n \\n```\\nPOST /api/public/scores\\n```\\nAdd scores via Python or JS SDK.\\nExample (Python)\\n \\n \\n```\\nlangfuse.score(\\n trace_id=\\\"123\\\",\\n name=\\\"my_custom_evaluator\\\",\\n value=0.5,\\n)\\n```\\n## Where to start?\\nSetting up the full process of online tracing, prompt management, production evaluations to identify issues, and offline evaluations on datasets requires some time. Most teams eventually end up with a process that looks like this:\\nDeploy\\n[OnlineTracetraces · sessions · agents · prompts](/academy/tracing)\\n[OnlineMonitordashboards · LLM-as-judge · feedback](/academy/monitoring)\\n[OfflineBuild datasetsdatasets · features-as-tests](/academy/datasets)\\n[OfflineExperimentprompts · models · code variants](/academy/experiments)\\n[OfflineEvaluatejudges · custom evals · annotation](/academy/evaluate)\\nIf you're new to AI engineering, take a look at the [Academy](/academy), where you'll find conceptual guidance on how to approach AI engineering, trade-offs, and best practices. If you already know what you want, the getting-started guides below will get you going.\\n💡\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nTip: let your coding agent do the setup and work with Langfuse through the [Agent Skill](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/agent-skill), [CLI](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/cli), or [MCP server](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/mcp-server). On Langfuse Cloud, you can also ask the [Langfuse Assistant](/docs/langfuse-assistant) about your project data from inside the app.\\n## Quickstarts\\nGet up and running with Langfuse in minutes. Choose the path that best fits your current needs:\\n[\\n### Integrate LLM Application/Agent Tracing\\n](/docs/observability/get-started)\\n[\\n### Integrate Prompt Management\\n](/docs/prompt-management/get-started)\\n[\\n### Setup Evaluations\\n](/docs/evaluation/overview)\\n## Why Langfuse?\\n * **Open source:** Fully open source with public API for custom integrations\\n * **Production optimized:** Designed with minimal performance overhead\\n * **Best-in-class SDKs:** Native SDKs for Python and JavaScript\\n * **Framework support:** Integrated with popular frameworks like OpenAI SDK, LangChain, and LlamaIndex\\n * **Multi-modal:** Support for tracing text, images and other modalities\\n * **Full platform:** Suite of tools for the complete LLM application development lifecycle\\n## Community & Contact\\nWe actively develop Langfuse in [open source](/open-source) together with our community:\\n * Contribute and vote on the Langfuse [roadmap](/docs/roadmap).\\n * Ask questions on [GitHub Discussions](/gh-support) or private [support channels](/support).\\n * Report bugs via [GitHub Issues](/issue).\\n * Chat with the community on [Discord](/discord).\\n * Join a [community hour](/events) to talk to the team and ask questions live.\\n * [Why people choose Langfuse?](/why)\\nLangfuse evolves quickly, check out the [changelog](/changelog) for the latest updates. Subscribe to the **mailing list** to get notified about new major features:\\nSubscribe\\n* * *\\n* * *\\nLast edited 9/1/2026\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"github_discussion\", \"url\": \"https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/9675\", \"title\": \"Self hosting Langfuse within our Cloud provider as a Highly available architecture\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Langfuse and most of its components can easily be run in a multi-availability-zone setup, but running it across multiple regions will be challenging (based on AWS definitions of AZs and regions). The guidelines in our self hosting documentation (https://langfuse.com/self-hosting#initialization) highlight which steps are necessary for a highly available deployment.\\r\\n\\r\\n> For the Click house DB hosted in the EKS cluster, is there a UI to access this Clickhouse instance by DBAs/DevOps for any data governance tasks for data within Clickhouse (say granting access to tables, views etc)?\\r\\n\\r\\nThere are many tools, e.g. DataGrip, that allow you to connect to the cluster and have a UI. I'm not aware of the clickhouse-server deployment shipping directly with an administrative interface.\\r\\n\\r\\n> Are there any best practices/schedule around patching/maintenance/upgrading of Langfuse and its components like Postgres, Redis, Clickhouse etc?\\r\\n\\r\\nWe recommend to regularly update to the latest version of Langfuse and apply security patches for other components.\\r\\n\\r\\n> If we consider using “Blob storage as disk” option in Click house instead of native Click house disk, will there be any performance implications in writes/reads? In other words, is there any scenario where using blob storage as disk may be better?\\r\\n\\r\\nPlease see our nodes on blob storage as disk here: https://langfuse.com/self-hosting/deployment/infrastructure/clickhouse#blob-storage-as-disk. We expect there to be a slightly higher latency on reads which may feel less snappy than a fully disk based architecture.\\r\\n\\r\\n> Langfuse human in the loop/evaluation addressing unsatisfactory response accuracy:\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"> > a. If we use the Langfuse evaluation feature - LLM as a judge, where the generation step (LLM generated) responses are evaluated, can we setup an automated process where responses are evaluated against a scoring rubric and scores are published?\\r\\nBasically, we want this automated evaluatio process to kick in only on generation step traces but not on all other traces.\\r\\n> > b. If we leverage a human in the loop evaluation, can we capture bad feedback responses and trigger a workflow outside of Langfuse?\\r\\nEg: For every bad feedback response, can we trigger a workflow where such responses are logged in any external application or JIRA APIs so these bad feedback responses are refined or flagged for respective teams to look into and address?\\r\\n\\r\\na.: Yes, you can apply granular filters during the LLM as a judge setup. I would recommend that you add some metadata to the traces that are relevant for you. We also plan to introduce generation-based LLM as a judge configurations that work on single generations instead of trace entities.\\r\\n\\r\\nb.: Currently, there are no webhooks based on scores or generations that would allow this. You'd have to export data from Langfuse on a regular basis. This is something that we plan to add.\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}]}"}

Great question. Langfuse is an open‑source AI engineering platform for building, debugging, and improving LLM apps and agents. It helps with:

  • Observability & tracing: Capture every prompt, model response, tool/retrieval step, latency, tokens, and errors to debug complex chains/agents Docs: Observability overview
  • Evaluation: Score output quality via LLM‑as‑a‑judge, code evaluators, human review, and user feedback—both on production traces (online) and datasets (offline) Docs: Evaluation overview, Core concepts
  • Prompt management: Version, release/rollback, test in a playground, and link prompts to traces and scores—update prompts without code deploys Docs: Prompt mgmt overview
  • Analytics, dashboards & alerts: Track quality, latency, cost, volume; alert on regressions (e.g., hallucination rate, error spikes) Docs: Custom dashboards, Alerts
  • Cost & token tracking: Break down usage and USD cost per model/provider Docs
  • Users, sessions, releases: Attribute traces to users/sessions, segment by env/version for safer rollouts Docs
  • OpenTelemetry-native & integrations: Works with Python/JS SDKs and 100+ frameworks/models; can ingest from existing OTel setups Docs
  • Deployment & security: Cloud or self-hosted (MIT OSS), with enterprise options and compliance controls Overview, Security, Self-hosting

Try it quickly:

  • Set up your first trace: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started
  • Explore the platform overview: https://langfuse.com/docs
